          - paragraph [ref=e699]:
            - text: The International Year of Pulses 2016 was declared by the
            - link "Sixty-eighth session of the United Nations General Assembly" [ref=e700] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Sixty-eighth_session_of_the_United_Nations_General_Assembly
            - text: .
            - superscript [ref=e701]:
              - link "[41]" [ref=e702] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: "#cite_note-iyp-52"
            - text: The
            - link "Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations" [ref=e703] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Food_and_Agriculture_Organization_of_the_United_Nations
            - text: was nominated to facilitate the implementation of the year in collaboration with governments, relevant organizations, non-governmental organizations and other relevant stakeholders. Its aim was to heighten public awareness of the nutritional benefits of pulses as part of
            - link "sustainable food" [ref=e704] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Sustainable_food_systems
            - text: production aimed towards
            - link "food security" [ref=e705] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Food_security
            - text: and
            - link "nutrition" [ref=e706] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Nutrition
            - text: . The year created an opportunity to encourage connections throughout the food chain that would better use pulse-based proteins, further global production of pulses, better use
            - link "crop rotations" [ref=e707] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Crop_rotation
            - text: and address challenges in the global trade of pulses.
            - superscript [ref=e708]:
              - link "[41]" [ref=e709] [cursor=pointer]:

import json
from datetime import datetime
import time

# Wikipedia API endpoint
url = "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php"

params = {
    "action": "query",
    "list": "logevents",
    "letitle": "Legume",
    "lestart": "2022-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "leend": "2022-11-30T23:59:59Z",
    "leprop": "title|type|user|timestamp|comment|details",
    "format": "json"
}

print("Querying Wikipedia API for log events on 'Legume' page...")
print(f"Time period: {params['lestart']} to {params['leend']}")
print()

# Make the API request
response = requests.get(url, params=params)

if response.status_code == 200:
    data = response.json()
    
    # Check if we have log events
    if 'query' in data and 'logevents' in data['query']:
        log_events = data['query']['logevents']
        print(f"Found {len(log_events)} log events in the specified period")
        print()
        
        # Display all log events first
        print("=== ALL LOG EVENTS ===")
        for i, event in enumerate(log_events, 1):
            print(f"\n{i}. Type: {event.get('type', 'N/A')}")
            print(f"   Action: {event.get('action', 'N/A')}")
            print(f"   Timestamp: {event.get('timestamp', 'N/A')}")
            print(f"   User: {event.get('user', 'N/A')}")
            print(f"   Comment: {event.get('comment', 'N/A')}")
            if 'details' in event:
                print(f"   Details: {event.get('details', 'N/A')}")
        
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("\n=== FILTERING FOR POTENTIAL CONTENT POLICY VIOLATIONS ===")
        
        # Policy violation keywords to look for in comments
        policy_keywords = [
            "original research", "OR", "NOR",
            "verifiability", "verifiable", "V", 
            "neutral point of view", "NPOV", "POV", "biased",
            "no reliable sources", "reliable sources", "citation needed",
            "copyvio", "copyright violation", "plagiarism",
            "spam", "advertising", "promotion",
            "vandalism", "test edit",
            "sockpuppet", "sock puppet",
            "BLP", "biographies of living persons",
            "conflict of interest", "COI"
        ]
        
        # Log types that might indicate policy issues
        policy_log_types = ["protect", "delete", "tag", "edit", "content", "block", "abusefilter"]
        
        # Filter events
        policy_events = []
        for event in log_events:
            event_type = event.get('type', '').lower()
            comment = event.get('comment', '').lower()
            action = event.get('action', '').lower()
            
            # Check for policy keywords in comments
            keyword_match = any(keyword.lower() in comment for keyword in policy_keywords)
            
            # Check if log type is relevant
            type_match = any(log_type in event_type for log_type in policy_log_types)
            
            # Also check action for specific policy-related actions
            policy_actions = ["delete", "protect", "tag", "revert", "abusefilter"]
            action_match = any(policy_action in action for policy_action in policy_actions)
            
            if keyword_match or (type_match and action_match):
                policy_events.append(event)
        
        print(f"\nFound {len(policy_events)} log events potentially related to content policy violations")
        print()
        
        if policy_events:
            # Display filtered events with analysis
            for i, event in enumerate(policy_events, 1):
                print(f"\n{i}. Type: {event.get('type', 'N/A')}")
                print(f"   Action: {event.get('action', 'N/A')}")
                print(f"   Timestamp: {event.get('timestamp', 'N/A')}")
                print(f"   User: {event.get('user', 'N/A')}")
                
                comment = event.get('comment', '')
                print(f"   Comment: {comment}")
                
                # Highlight policy keywords found
                found_keywords = []
                for keyword in policy_keywords:
                    if keyword.lower() in comment.lower():
                        found_keywords.append(keyword)
                
                if found_keywords:
                    print(f"   Policy keywords detected: {', '.join(found_keywords)}")
                
                if 'details' in event:
                    print(f"   Details: {event.get('details', 'N/A')}")
                
                print(f"   Link: https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Special:Log&logid={event.get('logid', '')}")
        else:
            print("No log events found with clear content policy violation indicators")
            
        # Summary statistics
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("\n=== SUMMARY STATISTICS ===")
        
        # Count by type
        type_counts = {}
        for event in log_events:
            event_type = event.get('type', 'unknown')
            type_counts[event_type] = type_counts.get(event_type, 0) + 1
        
        print("\nLog events by type:")
        for event_type, count in sorted(type_counts.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True):
            print(f"  {event_type}: {count}")
        
        # Count by action
        action_counts = {}
        for event in log_events:
            action = event.get('action', 'unknown')
            action_counts[action] = action_counts.get(action, 0) + 1
        
        print("\nLog events by action:")
        for action, count in sorted(action_counts.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True):
            print(f"  {action}: {count}")
            
    else:
        print("No log events found in the response")
        print("Response data:", json.dumps(data, indent=2))
        
else:
    print(f"Error: API request failed with status code {response.status_code}")
    print(response.text)"}

function.name: PostgresManager
function.description: A database management agent responsible for inspecting, querying, and analyzing a PostgreSQL database. It can enumerate schemas and database objects, retrieve detailed metadata about tables and other objects, and execute SQL queries (with read-only restrictions when applicable). In addition, it supports query planning and performance analysis, including explaining query execution plans, identifying slow or resource-intensive queries, recommending indexes based on workloads or specific queries, and performing comprehensive database health checks covering caches, indexes, constraints, connections, and maintenance status.

function.name: DocumentAnalyzer
function.description: A comprehensive document-processing agent capable of extracting, analyzing, and structuring content from a wide range of local office files and text formats. Provides unified text extraction, table and media extraction, metadata collection, structural analysis, and multi-format output (Markdown/JSON/HTML/Text). Designed to deliver clean, organized results for downstream reasoning and further processing. It can extract embedded media as raw files or generate screenshots for visual spreadsheet elements, which are then passed to specialized agents for further analysis.

function.name: MediaAnalyzer

It provides OCR extraction, AI-based visual understanding, metadata inspection, audio transcription and trimming, video analysis and summarization, and key-frame extraction. Supports common formats across images (JPG/PNG/GIF/TIFF/WEBP …), audio (MP3/WAV/FLAC/AAC/OGG …), and video (MP4/AVI/MOV/MKV/WEBM …). GIF and video content are processed as multi-frame sequences—similar to video key-frame extraction—while static image formats are analyzed as single frames. Designed to perform assigned multimedia tasks efficiently and return clear, structured results.
